### Front line

According to the Ukrainian monitoring project DeepStateMap, Russian forces newly occupied 5.7 square kilometres of previously contested territory and contested an additional 7.2 square kilometres, with no Ukrainian counter-advances recorded. DeepStateMap noted that approximately 70% of the village of Rusyn Yar in the Kramatorsk raion of Donetsk Oblast fell into the newly occupied zone. 

The Russian Ministry of Defence claimed that its "Vostok" grouping used mortars and "Krasnopol" precision-guided artillery shells to strike Ukrainian strongpoints and reserves in Zaporizhzhia Oblast. The Russian ministry also reported that a "Grad" multiple launch rocket system (MLRS) crew destroyed a Ukrainian drone command post and launch sites in Sumy Oblast, while an "Uragan" MLRS destroyed a Ukrainian "Bohdana" self-propelled howitzer on the Lyman axis.

### Strikes and losses

Open-source visual tracking by GeoConfirmed documented fires and damage across several locations. On Ukrainian territory, reported Russian attacks damaged the "Simia" shopping centre in Odesa, set fire to a warehouse near Europark, and destroyed buildings belonging to a hospital surgical department following reported FAB-250 strikes. GeoConfirmed also reported that a Russian FPV drone killed an unnamed civilian man, and another fibre-optic-controlled FPV drone damaged a Ukrainian civilian armoured pickup truck. 

In Russian and Russian-occupied areas, GeoConfirmed noted fires at an "Ozon" facility in Adygeysk and the "JSC Orelmaslo" oil seed plant, as well as Ukrainian drone strikes hitting the "Phoenix" telecommunications building in occupied Donetsk and a Russian "Pantsir" air defence vehicle. The independent project WarSpotting documented the destruction of three Russian vehicles near Vnezapnoe (Kursk Oblast): two "Ulan" all-terrain vehicles and a "Kuryer" logistics unmanned ground vehicle. 

The Russian Ministry of Defence claimed its forces launched drone strikes against Ukrainian energy infrastructure, specifically alleging hits on the 750 kV Nalyvaikivka electrical substation in Kyiv Oblast and the 110 kV Chizhovka substation in Zhytomyr Oblast. It also claimed to have struck two dry cargo ships allegedly delivering military cargo in and near the port of Odesa, alongside attacks across 153 areas targeting transport infrastructure and drone facilities. Russian air defences claimed to have intercepted 709 Ukrainian drones overnight and an additional 46 during the day across multiple Russian regions. These claims remain unverified.

The Ukrainian Ministry of Defence reported October totals, claiming that Ukrainian forces struck 47 Russian ammunition and fuel depots, 27 command posts, and numerous air defence systems, while Ukrainian air defences allegedly intercepted over 8,000 missiles and strike drones over the course of the month.

### Official statements

The Ukrainian Ministry of Defence announced that Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara met with Norwegian Finance Minister Jens Stoltenberg to discuss countering Russian ballistic threats. Khmara stated that Ukraine is targeting Russian launchers and missile component factories, while seeking to scale deep strikes, expand F-16 capabilities, and build underground fortifications. Separately, the Ukrainian defence ministry issued a clarification regarding territorial recruitment centres, warning that intentional obstruction of military mobilisation carries prison sentences ranging from 5 to 15 years.

The Russian Ministry of Defence focused heavily on National Unity Day celebrations, publicising holiday greetings and ceremonies. It also reported that Defence Minister Andrey Belousov visited Kazakhstan, where he met Defence Minister Aidos Myrzakhmetov and approved a bilateral military cooperation plan for 2027.
